key_insight: Urban carbon intensity from solar-rich distributed energy can vary sharply across districts and time, so localized estimation is essential for accurate emission-aware control.
engineering_relevance: The work supports smarter operation of buildings, EV charging, and district heating by providing high-resolution carbon intensity inputs and a transferable surrogate model when detailed local data are unavailable.
method: Compute spatially and temporally resolved carbon intensity factors at urban-district scale.
Train surrogate models using limited municipality/grid-operator inputs aligned with census grid cells.
Compare decision-tree methods with a neural-network architecture for estimation accuracy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports carbon intensity values ranging from 0 to 316 g/kWh in one city at summer noon and up to 9% emission-estimation error when local variation is ignored.
watch_item: Transferability may weaken in regions with sparse or non-representative input data, especially outside densely built urban areas.
paper_title: Quantification and Surrogate Model Estimation of Spatial-Temporal Carbon Intensity Factors
